title: Wasmannia is Allomerus: taxonomy confounded by a shift to being a plant ant
content:
Abstract
Wasmannia Forel 1893 and Allomerus Mayr 1878 are 2 Neotropical ant genera with divergent morphology and natural history. Most Wasmannia species are moderately abundant to rare ants with poorly known habits, but Wasmannia auropunctata is a highly generalized and highly invasive pest ant, notorious for the negative impacts of introduced populations. In contrast, all known species of Allomerus are highly specialized inhabitants of domatia-bearing ant plants in Amazonian South America. Long thought to be distantly related, recent molecular evidence has suggested that they are closely related. Here, we use ultraconserved elements and low-coverage whole-genome sequencing to construct a phylogeny of 5 Wasmannia species and 2 Allomerus species, strongly supporting the paraphyly of Wasmannia with respect to Allomerus, and supported by the analysis of cytochrome oxidase I sequences. The generalized morphology and habits of W. auropunctata are a “bauplan” that is retained by several species of Wasmannia, while a few Wasmannia species and the Allomerus lineage have diverged, Allomerus strongly so. Allomerus is the older name, necessitating the new synonymization of Wasmannia under Allomerus. All Wasmannia species are transferred to Allomerus as new combinations.
